newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Channel 5 to delay launch.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Channel 5 to delay launch.

text.p: Britain's planned fifth terrestrial television channel suffered a setback on Wednesday when it announced that it had been forced to delay its launch by as much as six weeks.

Channel 5 spokeswoman Sally Osman said the new commercial channel would definitely miss the January 1, 1997 launch date and that the delay "may be four to six weeks". The hold-up follows an expansion of Channel 5's coverage area.

The government said this week that it was granting Channel 5 access to an additional frequency which would make it available in an extra 1.8 million homes -- boosting total coverage to over 80 percent of the United Kingdom.
The extra coverage creates more work for Channel 5's engineers who must visit millions of households nationwide to retune video recorders to prevent interference from its signal.
"We want to make sure we get everything right," said Osman, stressing that Channel 5 wanted to complete the retuning process before it goes on air.
Osman said Channel 5 was redrafting its retuning plan and that it did not have a revised target date for the launch.
Channel 5 Broadcasting is a consortium comprising British media companies Pearson and United News & Media plus broadcast group CLT of Luxembourg and U.S. investment firm Warburg Pincus.

Pearson said recently that the retuning process would cost some 100 million pounds ($155 million). That figure is likely to rise now that an extra 1.8 million households have to be added to the budget.

Critics of the retuning plan have dubbed it a "thieves' charter" and the British Retail Consortium, which represents many high street stores, has voiced concern that it could invalidate product guarantees.
